newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ruggiero says to name Helms-Burton disputes panel.
newsitem.headline: Ruggiero says to name Helms-Burton disputes panel.

text.p: World Trade Organisation head Renato Ruggiero said on Tuesday he had received a formal request from the European Union to name a disputes panel on its row with Washington over the Helms-Burton Act and said he would do so in the coming days.
But he declined to say whether this step, required under WTO rules, would automatically bring about a WTO enquiry into the legislation.
The United States regards the legislation, meant to punish investment by foreign companies in Cuba, as a matter of national security and outside the powers of the Geneva-based WTO.
"I was officially informed of this request (the EU request) last night. As soon as I return to Geneva on Thursday, I will start to think about the membership of a panel.
"I have to make a decision within 10 days," Ruggiero told reporters after a hearing at the French Senate.

Asked whether choosing the membership of a disputes panel would automatically set the WTO disputes procedure in motion, Ruggiero said that this was outside his responsibility which was limited to naming the panel.
"This step by Brussels requests me to name the members of a panel, no more than that," he said.
"Now my responsibility is to name the panel, which is what I will do. After that we will see. For the moment I cannot go beyond my own responsibilities," he said.

The United States and European Union have been unable to agree since November on the composition of a three-person panel to rule whether Brussels is correct in complaining the Helms-Burton Act constitutes restraint of trade and falls under the WTO's remit.
A spokesman for EU Trade Commissioner Leon Brittan said on Monday that Brussels would seek to break the deadlock by asking Ruggiero himself to choose the members of a panel.
